interest: This file is particularly valuable to historians as an administrative and intelligence roadmap documenting U.S. surveillance and diplomatic handling of the Imperial Japanese Navy's buildup in the critical period immediately preceding and during World War II. It illustrates pre-war FBI and ONI counterintelligence investigations into Japanese petroleum purchasing and the operations of Japanese naval inspectors stationed in Los Angeles and New York. Additionally, the docket reveals U.S. inter-agency intelligence sharing—tracking secret Japanese naval construction, warship launchings, and battleship building programs between 1937 and 1941, followed by wartime intelligence gathered in Chungking regarding the repair and reconditioning of Japanese naval vessels. The cross-reference notations also offer significant archival utility by directing researchers to the specific related decimal files (such as 811.34/1086, 894.20211, and 894.642) where primary documents were transferred or classified.
overview: This file consists of two consecutive docket sheets of the Department of State's List of Papers (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.34, cataloguing records relating to equipment and supplies for the Japanese Navy between February 1940 and March 1944. The entries document U.S. diplomatic and intelligence surveillance of Japanese naval expansion and procurement operations, beginning with reports from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo regarding Japanese naval building plans and statements by the Japanese Navy Minister. It records domestic counterintelligence investigations by the Justice Department and FBI Special Agent R.B. Hood into Japanese oil purchasing and subversive activities in Los Angeles, along with communications and State Department conferences with the Japanese Embassy regarding the movements and official permissions of Japanese naval inspectors from New York operating in California. The file also tracks Department of Justice reports concerning Japanese industrial shipbuilding capacity, naval vessel launchings from 1937 to 1940, and capital warship construction, concluding with March 1944 despatches from Ambassador Clarence E. Gauss in Chungking transmitting intelligence memoranda on the reconditioning of Japanese naval vessels. Throughout, cross-reference notations trace the routing and transfer of these documents to related State Department decimal files.

subfiles.about: A two-page Department of State List of Papers docket indexing correspondence, intelligence memoranda, and diplomatic notes concerning Japanese naval equipment, construction, and inspection activities between 1940 and 1944.
subfiles.summary: This sub-file comprises two continuation sheets of Form DS-46 (List of Papers) for State Department decimal file 894.34, cataloguing records relating to Japanese naval equipment, supplies, and shipbuilding between February 1940 and March 1944. The docket registers reports from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo regarding Japanese naval expansion and statements by the Navy Minister, along with Justice Department and FBI reports by Special Agent R.B. Hood investigating subversive activities and oil purchasing in Los Angeles. It details State Department discussions with the Japanese Embassy concerning the temporary assignment of Japanese naval inspectors from New York to Los Angeles, as well as Justice Department intelligence memoranda on Japanese shipbuilding capacity, launchings between 1937 and 1940, and battleship construction. The register concludes with March 1944 despatches from Ambassador Clarence E. Gauss in Chungking transmitting memoranda on the reconditioning of Japanese naval vessels, with numerous notations recording the cross-referencing or transfer of underlying documents to related decimal files.
